cover.headline: The gRevlimid years are over; semaglutide and abatacept are late, and the price already allows for both
cover.lead: Dr. Reddy's is a ₹34,000 cr generics company that is half branded (India, Russia and emerging markets, Nicotinell) and half unbranded (US and European generics, APIs). FY23-FY25 were windfall years: generic Revlimid lifted EBITDA margins to 26-28% and EPS to ₹68. The windfall ended in Jan-2026: Q4FY26 EPS was ₹2.6 and Q1FY27 ₹5.3, after a ₹240 cr provision when the semaglutide API failed validation at scale and supplies stopped until ~Nov-2026. The street values Dr. Reddy's on **P/E on one-year-forward EPS (20-23x FY28E)**. We forecast EPS of ₹35.7 / ₹51.7 / ₹62.9 for FY27-29E, below the street on margins. Dr. Reddy's own forward P/E since Apr-2021 has a median of 19.6x on EPS before one-offs; times the pharma sector factor (+8.2%) that gives **21x Sep-28E EPS of ₹57.3 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**. **We initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks agree within ±15% (EV/EBITDA ₹1,369, DCF ₹1,141). Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: North America has fallen off the cliff and is not growing underneath
arguments.p: US$ sales went from US$400 mn in Q1FY26 to US$236 mn in Q1FY27 as lenalidomide went generic. The base left behind (~US$950 mn a year) is about where it was in FY22 despite ~100 launches; the CEO concedes R&D misses in complex generics. Bosutinib and sugammadex (first to market in 2026) help FY27; after that, growth needs semaglutide in Canada and abatacept. We model US1,060 / 1,200 / 1,300 mn for FY27-29E.

arguments.h: The branded half is good and growing
arguments.p: India grew 17% in Q1FY27 (15.5% organic) against a market growing 13.5%; emerging markets +31% (Russia +28%, Rest of World +42%); Nicotinell (bought from Haleon for GBP458 mn) grows high single digit to low double digit. These businesses were 52% of Q1FY27 revenue and carry the margin today.

arguments.h: Two big launches, both delayed once already
arguments.p: Semaglutide: first to market in India and Canada, then an API scale-up failure in Jul-2026; 6-7 mn pens promised for Nov-26 to Mar-27 (was 10-11 mn). Abatacept (biosimilar Orencia): goal date mid-Dec-2026; the biologics plant passed muster for rituximab in Aug-2026. We include ~₹1,500 cr of semaglutide in FY27E and US$80 mn of abatacept in FY28E: real, but below management's plan.

arguments.h: Valuation: fair on the street's own method
arguments.p: At ₹1,233 the stock trades at 23.8x our FY28E EPS and 21.5x Sep-28E, against a 19.6x median since 2021 (25th-75th percentile 15.7-23.7x). The post-Q1 street median target is ₹1,222 (range ₹1,040-1,740). Our 21x is in the middle of the street's 20-23x; the debate is earnings, not the multiple.

catalysts: Semaglutide re-validation result (management targeted around 22-23 Sep-2026) and the restart of commercial supplies via OneSource from Oct, pens to market from Nov-2026; Brazil approval (expected "in the next few weeks" in Jul-2026).

Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026; the company's calendar says the fourth week of October): the first quarter with bosutinib exclusivity and sugammadex, and the base margin without semaglutide ("neighbourhood of 20%" IFRS guided).
Abatacept IV: US FDA goal date mid-December 2026; response to the Bachupally Form 483; EU IV filing; SC filing in the US.
Use of the ~₹3,000 cr net cash: management is "engaging" on deals in generics, innovation and biosimilars.
US tariff on generics (announced 22-Jul-2026) and USFDA follow-up at Srikakulam (Form 483, 3 observations, Jul-2026).

sections.title: A generics company with four markets and an API arm, turning itself into a branded and biologics business

blocks.p: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories, founded in Hyderabad in 1984, makes generic medicines and their active ingredients (APIs). It is the only Indian drug maker listed on the New York Stock Exchange (since 2001). It reports two segments. **Global Generics** (89% of FY26 revenue) sells finished medicines in North America, Europe, India and emerging markets. **PSAI** (10%) sells APIs to other drug makers and runs contract development and manufacturing (CDMO). Branded businesses, where doctors prescribe a Dr. Reddy's brand (India, emerging markets and the nicotine-replacement consumer brands bought from Haleon), were 52% of Q1FY27 revenue.

blocks.callout: **So what:** strip out lenalidomide and Dr. Reddy's is a diversified mid-teens-margin generics company whose growth now comes from branded markets (India, Russia and Rest of World, NRT), not the US. Its big bets for FY27-FY29 are three products: generic semaglutide (outside the US), biosimilar abatacept (US) and a rebuilt US generics launch engine. Each is binary in timing; together they decide whether margins return to 20%+ on our basis.

sections.title: Three different industries: price-taking US generics, a 11-13%-growth Indian brand market, and branded emerging markets

blocks.p: **US generics.** The world's largest generics market is a price-taker business: a few large buyer groups force prices down every year, and excess profit comes only from products with few competitors (first-to-file exclusivity, complex injectables, settlements like lenalidomide's). Dr. Reddy's grew 10.3% excluding lenalidomide against 2.1% for the market (IQVIA MAT Jun-2026), helped by launches. Its CEO is candid: "the US market, the generic piece of it, is at best single-digit growth, without the upsides". A new risk appeared on 22-Jul-2026, when the US President announced tariffs on generic medicines; 25-30% of Dr. Reddy's US sales are made by US contract manufacturers.

**India.** The Indian pharmaceutical market (IPM) grew 11.1% on a moving annual basis and 13.5% in the quarter to Jun-2026, mostly through price and new products. Dr. Reddy's grew 13.5% / 14.6% and ranks #9-10. The biggest new profit pool is semaglutide: Novo Nordisk's patent expired in Mar-2026 and several Indian companies launched on day one; Dr. Reddy's had ~10% share in its first weeks (May-2026).

**Emerging markets and Canada.** Russia (Dr. Reddy's grew 10.9% vs 15.2% for the market, IQVIA May-2026), CIS and 40+ Rest-of-World countries are branded markets where a company sells its own brands to doctors and pharmacies. Generic semaglutide opens 80+ such markets in 2026-27 as data protection and patents lapse; Canada was first (Dr. Reddy's approval in Q4FY26, launch in Q1FY27). In Canada the list price is ~CAD78 a pen, retailers keep ~38% and provinces take another 5-6%; management expects net prices of US$30+ a pen and not below US$25.

bullets: **GLP-1 genericisation outside the US:** semaglutide loses protection in India, Canada, Brazil and many emerging markets in 2026-27; demand far exceeds supply and few companies make the peptide API in-house.

**Biosimilars:** the US FDA's draft guidance (raised on the Q4FY26 call) lowers the cost of developing biosimilars, and Dr. Reddy's first US targets (abatacept/Orencia, denosumab/Prolia) are large biologics with few or no biosimilars yet.
**The rupee:** ₹95.81/US$ on 30-Sep-2026 vs ~₹87.5 average in FY26; about 80% of revenue is earned outside India.

**The end of limited-competition windfalls:** gRevlimid volume limits ended in Jan-2026 and prices collapsed (Dr. Reddy's took a ₹453 cr shelf-stock adjustment); US base erosion is single digit to low double digit a year.

**Execution and regulation:** the semaglutide API scale-up failed validation in Jul-2026; USFDA observations at Bachupally (biologics, 7) and Srikakulam (3) in Jun-Jul 2026; any OAI can stall launches.
**Geopolitics and costs:** Russia sanctions and rouble swings; the Middle East conflict raised solvent and freight costs by ~1 point of margin in Q1FY27; US tariff threat on generics.

sections.title: North America: the gRevlimid cliff has happened; the base is ~US$950 mn a year and barely growing

blocks.p: North America was ₹11,374 cr (US$1.30 bn) in FY26, down 22%, and US$236 mn in Q1FY27, down 41% YoY. The reason is one product. **Generic Revlimid** (lenalidomide, a blood-cancer drug) was sold from FY23 under settlements that capped every generic maker's volumes; the caps ended in Jan-2026 and prices fell. Dr. Reddy's sales fell from US$400 mn a quarter (Q1FY26) to US$338 mn (Q3) and US$251 mn (Q4, before a ₹453 cr, ~US$50 mn shelf-stock adjustment that a customer claimed for stock it held when prices dropped; the CEO said "we were also surprised by that"). The company never disclosed lenalidomide's sales. What is left is a US generics base that an IIFL analyst put at ~US$1 bn in FY22 and ~US$950 mn annualised now despite 90-100 launches and the Mayne portfolio; the CEO agreed: "if you take out product like lenalidomide, your analysis is correct".

sections.title: Semaglutide: first to market in Canada and India, then an API failure; 6-7 mn pens promised for Nov-Mar

blocks.p: Semaglutide (Novo Nordisk's Ozempic/Wegovy molecule) is the largest generic opportunity of 2026-27 outside the US. Dr. Reddy's makes the peptide API itself by chemical synthesis (the originator uses recombinant DNA), which gives it cost and supply control, and fills pens through partners (OneSource). It was first to approval in India (Nov-2025; brand Obeda launched on the day the patent expired in Mar-2026) and in Canada (approval in Q4FY26, launch in Q1FY27), and has filed in ~30 countries of an 80-country programme. In May-2026 it guided ~12 mn pens for FY27 and 6-7 mn by Dec-2026.

Then, on 9-Jul-2026, it disclosed that an impurity in the API from a scaled-up process went out of specification in the finished product during validation. Supplies stopped. Management found the root cause, put the success odds of re-validation at "80% to 90%", targeted completion around 22-23 Sep-2026, and now expects 6-7 mn pens between Nov-2026 and Mar-2027 (backed by orders), not 10-11 mn. Q1FY27 carried a ₹240 cr provision for unusable inventory and costs; only ~180,000 pens were sold. The oral tablets (launched in India in Q1FY27) use a different API and are unaffected. A backup API supplier needs a prior-approval supplement, about a year away.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is a good franchise hurt by a self-inflicted delay. The lost four months cost Dr. Reddy's its head start in Canada, where Apotex keeps selling while Dr. Reddy's and its partner wait for API. We include ₹1,500 cr of semaglutide revenue in FY27E and ₹2,450 cr in FY28E, below management's run-rate. sections.title: Biosimilars: abatacept is the prize (goal date mid-Dec-2026); the biologics plant passed its first US approval in Aug-2026

blocks.p: Dr. Reddy's has spent years and much of its R&D budget on biosimilars (copies of biological drugs). Global biologics sales are only ~US$100 mn (about 2% of revenue) and not yet profitable. The pivot is **abatacept** (biosimilar Orencia, for rheumatoid arthritis): the intravenous (IV) version's BLA was accepted in Feb-2026 with a mid-December 2026 goal date, the subcutaneous (SC) version follows around Feb/Mar-2028 in the US. In June 2026 the FDA's pre-licence inspection of the Bachupally biologics plant (which covered abatacept and rituximab) ended with seven observations; on 1-Aug-2026 the FDA approved Dr. Reddy's **rituximab** biosimilar after that inspection. Management hopes for US$500-700 mn of biosimilar sales by FY29, "the lion's share" from abatacept.

sections.title: India and emerging markets: 39% of revenue, growing 15-30%, and the steadiest part of the business

blocks.p: **India** revenue was ₹6,219 cr in FY26 (+16%) and ₹1,718 cr in Q1FY27 (+17%; 15.5% organic, i.e. excluding acquired brands). Dr. Reddy's out-grew the market on IQVIA data (14.6% vs 13.5% in the quarter to Jun-2026) and ranks #9-10. The drivers are specific: in-licensed innovation (toripalimab, a PD-1 cancer drug, passed ₹100 cr in under two years), new launches (28 brands in FY26, 7 in Q1FY27), price increases, vaccines (#2) and bought brands (Progynova and Cyclo-Progynova in hormone therapy, Stugeron). Semaglutide (Obeda injection, oral tablets) added little in Q1 because of the supply halt. Its biggest brands (Atarax ₹274 cr, Ketorol ₹265 cr, Econorm ₹249 cr MAT Jun-2026) grow 10-20%.

**Emerging Markets** grew from ₹4,567 cr (FY22) to ₹6,761 cr (FY26) and +31% in Q1FY27 to ₹1,833 cr: Russia ₹903 cr (+28%, price increases, launches and a stronger rouble), other CIS and Romania ₹219 cr (+12%), Rest of World ₹710 cr (+42%). The model is to take products developed for the US and launch them across 48 countries (129 launches in FY26, 43 in Q1FY27), plus in-licensed brands (XACDURO, tegoprazan). Adjusted for currency, Elara estimates Russia/CIS grew only low single digits in Q1FY27, and IQVIA shows Dr. Reddy's growing slower than the Russian market (10.9% vs 15.2%).

sections.title: Europe, NRT and the Nestle venture: a bought consumer franchise that works, and a nutrition JV still losing money

blocks.p: **Europe** jumped from ₹3,588 cr (FY25) to ₹5,550 cr (FY26, +55%; +14% excluding NRT) and was ₹1,444 cr in Q1FY27 (+13%). It has two parts. Generics in Germany (₹407 cr in Q1FY27, +29%), the UK (₹231 cr, +33%), France, Italy and Spain grew on launches (24 in Q1FY27) and a stronger euro against price erosion. **NRT** (nicotine replacement therapy: Nicotinell, Nicabate, Thrive, Habitrol) was bought from Haleon for GBP458 mn upfront plus up to GBP42 mn of earn-out (completed 30-Sep-2024); Nicotinell is the #2 NRT brand outside the US. NRT revenue was ₹656 cr in Q1FY27 (−2% YoY) because, after integration ended in Mar-2026, rebates to distributors are now deducted from revenue (profit-neutral, with lower SG&A). Management says NRT grows high single digit to low double digit with a "very healthy" margin.

**Consumer health and nutrition.** In Apr-2024 Dr. Reddy's and Nestle India agreed to form "Dr. Reddy's and Nestle Health Science Limited" (Dr. Reddy's 51%, Nestle India 49%) to sell nutraceuticals in India: Nestle licensed Nature's Bounty, Osteo Bi-Flex and Ester-C; Dr. Reddy's transferred Celevida, Rebalanz, Antoxid, Kidrich-D3 and Becozinc (receiving ₹811 cr in FY25). In 2026 it launched Celevida GLP+, nutrition for patients on GLP-1 drugs, alongside the semaglutide launch. The JV lost money in FY26: Nestle's 49% absorbed a ₹38 cr loss (Dr. Reddy's share ~₹40 cr). Management runs consumer health as a separate pillar under its own head.

sections.title: PSAI: a ₹3,500 cr API and CDMO arm with thin margins, now carrying the semaglutide API

blocks.p: PSAI (Pharmaceutical Services and Active Ingredients) sells APIs to other generic makers and runs contract development and manufacturing. Revenue was ₹3,198 cr in FY21 and ₹3,477 cr in FY26 (+3%): it has barely grown in five years. Gross margin was 17.2% in FY26 (27% in FY25, 23% in FY24 on the five-year summary) and 4.5% in Q1FY27 (12.9% excluding the semaglutide API provision). It filed 128 drug master files in FY26 and 38 in Q1FY27. PSAI makes the semaglutide API for Dr. Reddy's own pens and for other generic companies (management: "plenty of capacity for both third parties as well as ourselves").

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Dr. Reddy's has no wide moat. Its excess profits in FY23-FY25 came from one time-limited US product. What it does have is a good, diversified branded-generics business (India, Russia, Rest of World, NRT) worth ~half of revenue, real chemistry skill in complex APIs, and a strong balance sheet. Biosimilars could become a moat if abatacept succeeds; today they are a cost. In US generics, by the CEO's own account, R&D productivity lagged peers for years.

sections.title: Revenue up 1.8x since FY21; profit rode gRevlimid to FY25 and fell back in FY26-27

blocks.p: Dr. Reddy's grew revenue from ₹19,048 cr in FY21 to ₹33,700 cr in FY26 (Ind AS, about 12% a year). Profit did something very different. EBITDA (Screener basis: before other income, after impairments) went from ₹3,768 cr in FY22 to ₹8,547 cr in FY25 and the margin from 17.5% to 26-28%, because generic Revlimid (gRevlimid, lenalidomide) was sold in the US under volume-limited settlements with few competitors. EPS more than doubled from ₹26.2 (FY22) to ₹67.8 (FY25). Profit attributable to shareholders was ₹15,740 cr in FY23-FY25, 2.6x the ₹6,160 cr of FY20-FY22. In FY26 the windfall ended: North America fell 22%, EBITDA fell to ₹6,454 cr (19.2%) and EPS to ₹50.3, including about ₹1,100 cr of one-off charges. Q1FY27 EPS was ₹5.32.

blocks.p: A word on bases first. Dr. Reddy's reports and guides on **IFRS EBITDA**, which includes other operating income (brand divestment gains, settlements, licence income) and forex, and excludes impairments: 22.8% in FY26 (24.7% before the specific items) and 12.5% in Q1FY27 (15.4% before the semaglutide provision). sections.title: The gRevlimid cash went into capacity, biologics, NRT and in-licensing; returns have halved

blocks.p: Over FY21-26 Dr. Reddy's generated ₹27,129 cr of operating cash flow, spent ₹15,072 cr on fixed assets (₹10,024 cr of it in FY24-26, building biologics, peptide and injectable capacity) and paid ₹3,325 cr of dividends. It also spent heavily on deals and licences: the Haleon NRT business (GBP458 mn upfront, ~₹5,141 cr, Sep-2024), Mayne Pharma's US generics portfolio, Indian brands (Progynova, Cyclo-Progynova, Stugeron) and in-licensed innovation (toripalimab, tegoprazan, XACDURO). Net cash fell from ₹5,369 cr (Mar-23, Screener basis) to ₹900 cr (Mar-26); the company's own "net cash surplus", which also counts term deposits and excludes leases, was ₹3,271 cr at Mar-26 and ₹3,057 cr at Jun-26.

sections.title: Net cash ₹3,057 cr, but working capital is 43% of revenue and borrowings are rising

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 Dr. Reddy's had ₹37,892 cr of equity attributable to shareholders and ₹339 cr of minority interest (Nestle India's 49% of the nutraceutical JV). Against it: goodwill ₹1,480 cr and other intangibles ₹10,506 cr (NRT brands, in-licensed products, acquired Indian brands), inventories ₹7,653 cr and receivables ₹10,123 cr. Operating working capital (inventory + receivables − payables) was ₹14,434 cr, ~43% of revenue, and ₹14,353 cr at Jun-26. Gross cash and investments were ₹9,851 cr against ₹7,734 cr of borrowings (₹6,294 cr short-term, ₹1,441 cr leases). The short-term loans have grown from ₹1,119 cr (Mar-23) as the company funds working capital and keeps an interest carry on its deposits.

sections.title: The street: split down the middle, targets ₹1,040-1,740, all disclosed methods on P/E

blocks.p: 19 houses published targets after the Q1FY27 results (22-24 Jul-2026), from ₹1,040 (Citi, Jefferies) to ₹1,740 (Nomura): median ₹1,222, −1% vs the 30-Sep-2026 close of ₹1,233. Ratings split roughly evenly between Buy (ICICI Direct, BOB, Nuvama, and by target Investec and Nomura), Hold/Neutral (MOSL, Macquarie, Morgan Stanley) and Sell/Reduce (Elara, Emkay, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Citi). Every note that discloses a method uses **P/E on one-year-forward EPS** (20-23x FY28E or 12-month-forward EPS; Elara 28x FY28E "core" EPS plus cash). The stock fell ~9% the day after the results. No broker values Dr. Reddy's as a sum of parts or on EV/EBITDA.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Dr. Reddy's Laboratories (consolidated, Ind AS basis as on Screener, Rs crore). The company reports and guides on IFRS; the business-line build uses IFRS segment revenue plus a reconciliation line to Ind AS revenue (Rs107 cr in FY26). The engine runs on one revenue path and one EBITDA margin on Screener's basis (Ind AS operating profit: excludes other income, i.e. interest, mutual-fund gains, forex and divestment gains, and is after impairments; FY26 19.2% vs 22.8% IFRS EBITDA). Profit is attributable to equity holders (DRREDDY.patch.js); the tax line carries tax less the minority's share of losses in the Nestle nutraceutical JV (built in `taxBuild`). Other income is built in `otherIncomeBuild`: treasury income at 6.5% on gross yield-earning cash (the engine applies the yield to its opening net cash; the yield on the gross borrowings held as cash, plus forex, recurring miscellaneous income and the JV share, sit in `otherIncome`). Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the business-line build (`businessLines`), checked against model revenue in tools/authoring/DRREDDY.ctx.js. FY26 IFRS revenue Rs33,593 cr (NA Rs11,374 cr after the Rs453 cr lenalidomide SSA, Europe Rs5,550 cr, India Rs6,219 cr, EM Rs6,761 cr, PSAI Rs3,477 cr, others Rs213 cr; ar26 table 1) + Rs107 cr to Ind AS Rs33,700 cr. FY27E +4.2% to Rs35,106 cr: Q1FY27 Rs8,100 cr (Ind AS, -5.5% YoY) is the trough; bosutinib and sugammadex first-to-market launches from Q2, semaglutide back from Nov-2026 (6-7 mn pens guided Nov-Mar; we assume ~5 mn, ~Rs1,500 cr across segments), India +15%, EM +17% with a weaker rupee. Street FY27E: MOSL Rs34,653 cr, PL Rs34,505 cr, Elara Rs35,371 cr, Emkay Rs35,288 cr, ICICI Direct Rs34,335 cr (Ind AS). FY28E +11.8%: a full year of semaglutide (~Rs2,450 cr), abatacept's first year in the US (~US$80 mn), India +12%; FY29E +10.0%: abatacept US$180 mn incl. the SC launch (Feb/Mar-2028), semaglutide price erosion offset by volume.
assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (Ind AS operating profit, excludes other income, after impairments). History: 23.0% FY23, 28.3% FY24, 26.2% FY25, 19.2% FY26 (22.4% before the SSA, VAT, labour-code and impairment items), 4.7% in Q4FY26 (14.7% before them), 10.6% in Q1FY27 (13.6% before the Rs240 cr semaglutide provision; ~1 point of Middle East freight and solvent costs). Management's 'neighbourhood of 20%' is IFRS EBITDA, which also includes other operating income and forex (about 1.5-2 points more than our basis) and ignores the Q1 provision. FY27E 16.0%: Q1 10.6% actual, then a 15-16% base with bosutinib exclusivity in Q2-Q3 and semaglutide's high contribution in Q3-Q4 (ICICI Direct Ind AS FY27E 16.3%; Elara IFRS 15.8%, MOSL 16.0%, PL 17.3%, Emkay 17.8%). FY29E 20.0%: abatacept scales; semaglutide prices fall as competitors enter.
assumptions._capexWhy: Management guided ~Rs1,800 cr for FY27 and 'around that range' after (22-Jul-2026 call; Rs2,000 cr guided in May; Rs2,302 cr in FY26, Rs3,440 cr in FY25 on Screener). Q1FY27 Rs307 cr (cash). Peptide and biologics capacity is already built (fill-finish, CCM5).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A Rs2,059 cr (Ind AS: depreciation Rs1,260 cr + amortisation Rs799 cr, ar26 note 2.19) = 5.1% of average gross block (Rs40,307 cr on Screener). assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (short-term borrowings incl. packing credit, leases)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs374 cr (other borrowings Rs269 cr, leases Rs80 cr, long-term Rs24 cr; ar26 note 2.20); Q1FY27 Rs125.5 cr (Rs502 cr annualised) on borrowings of Rs7,195 cr at Jun-26 (short-term Rs5,769 cr, leases Rs1,426 cr). Borrowings are held flat at ~Rs7,200 cr (the short-term loans fund working capital and an interest carry on deposits), so finance cost stays ~Rs480-490 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax less the minority's share of JV losses (engine has no minority line). Built in `taxBuild`: tax at 24% / 25% / 25% of PBT (guidance 24-25% for FY27; Q1FY27 21.3% on a tax-provision reversal; FY26 22.5%, FY25 25.4% IFRS) less Nestle India's 49% share of the nutraceutical JV's losses, Rs30 / 20 / 10 cr (FY26 Rs38.4 cr loss to the minority, Q1FY27 Rs8.7 cr). Checked each year in DRREDDY.ctx.js.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend of Rs8 a share for FY25 and FY26 (Rs668 cr, 16% of FY26 profit; 12% of FY25). We assume Rs8 / Rs9 / Rs10 a share (about 20% / 16% / 15% of our EPS). No buyback since 2016-17.

businessLines._note: Revenue build by market (Rs crore; North America in US$ mn x Rs/US$). FY26 base from ar26 MD&A table 1 (IFRS); 'indasRecon' bridges IFRS to Ind AS revenue (FY26 Rs33,700.2 cr - Rs33,593.3 cr). Checked against model revenue in DRREDDY.ctx.js (tolerance 0.5%).

memo._why: GAM estimates inside the market lines (not disclosed by the company): semaglutide ~5 mn pens in Nov-26 to Mar-27 at ~US$31 net (management: 6-7 mn pens, US$25-30+ a pen, list price ~half of Novo's), then ~15 mn pens a year at falling prices; abatacept (biosimilar Orencia IV) from a mid-Dec-2026 goal date with a slow first-year ramp, SC from Feb/Mar-2028.

businessLines._why: North America (US$): FY26 US$1,300 mn reported (US$1,360 mn before the SSA); Q1FY27 US$236 mn with ~2 weeks of bosutinib. FY27E US$1,060 mn = base generics ~US$950 mn (Q1 run-rate; 'double-digit growth ex-lenalidomide' guided) + bosutinib (180-day exclusivity, brand ~US$300 mn) and sugammadex (first to market, 28-Jul-2026) + Canada semaglutide ~US$70 mn; MOSL US$1,066 mn, Emkay Rs10,449 cr. FY28E US$1,200 mn (Canada semaglutide ~US$120 mn, abatacept ~US$80 mn; bosutinib exclusivity over), FY29E US$1,300 mn (abatacept US$180 mn). Rs/US$ 95.6 / 97.5 / 99.5 (95.81 on 30-Sep-2026; Q1FY27 convenience rate 94.66). Europe: Q1FY27 Rs1,444 cr (+13% YoY, NRT Rs656 cr after a profit-neutral gross-to-net change); +9% / +8% / +8% (NRT high single digit to low double digit; generics launches vs price erosion; strong euro). India: Q1FY27 +17% (15.5% organic) vs IPM +13.5% MQT; +15% / +12% / +12% incl. semaglutide (injection and oral). Emerging Markets: FY26 +23%, Q1FY27 +31% (Russia +28%, RoW +42%, forex); +17% / +12% / +10% incl. semaglutide B2B supplies in new markets. PSAI: Q1FY27 +4% (CDMO up, API volumes down); +5% / +8% / +8%. Others (licensing, services): Rs213 cr in FY26, Rs19 cr in Q1FY27; Rs100 cr a year.

otherIncomeBuild._note: Engine other income = 6.5% x opening engine net cash (treasuryYield) + otherIncome; otherIncome = carry + forex + misc + jv (Rs crore).
otherIncomeBuild._why: FY26 Ind AS other income Rs1,358.4 cr + JV Rs13.4 cr = Rs1,371.8 cr; excluding the Rs189 cr brand divestment gain and the Rs140 cr litigation settlement: Rs1,042.8 cr (ar26 note 2.16). Twelve months to Jun-26 (Screener quarters Rs330 + 271 + 480 + 356 cr = Rs1,437 cr incl. JV) less the same two items and ~Rs66 cr of other disposal gains: ~Rs1,040 cr. Non-yielding stakes: equity-accounted investees Rs567 cr (Mar-26) + equity investments Rs315 cr (q1pr net-cash reconciliation).

taxBuild._note: Engine tax rate = (tax on PBT + minority share of JV profit, negative when the JV loses money) / PBT.
taxBuild._why: Nestle India owns 49% of 'Dr. Reddy's and Nestle Health Science Limited' (ar26 note 2.39 A). The minority absorbed Rs38.4 cr of losses in FY26 and Rs8.7 cr in Q1FY27 (IFRS NCI Rs-87 mn); we assume the JV's losses narrow as Celevida GLP+ and the licensed Nestle brands scale.

dcf._betaWhy: Pharma is defensive; Dr. Reddy's has net cash (Rs3,057 cr at Jun-26), so the cost of equity is the right discount rate. Beta 0.85 gives 11.6%.
dcf._tgWhy: India nominal GDP ~10%; half the business is unbranded generics (US, Europe, PSAI) growing low single digits in dollars, half branded (India, EM, NRT) growing high single digits. House range 5-6%: 5.5%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% (FY29E) to 7% over 15 years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Screener-basis EBITDA margin fades from 20% to 21%: the branded mix rises and biosimilars add margin, but US generic erosion and semaglutide price competition recur; we do not assume the 26-28% of the gRevlimid years.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex moves from ~4% of revenue (FY29E) to 5%: maintenance plus biologics and peptide capacity for a ~Rs40,000 cr business (FY23-FY26 capex 7-10% of revenue included the biologics build-out).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Semaglutide restarts on time in Nov-2026 and sells 7 mn+ pens in H2FY27 and 20 mn+ in FY28 across Canada, Brazil and 50+ markets; abatacept is approved in Dec-2026 with little competition; the US base holds ~US$1 bn; EBITDA margin heads to the 25% aspiration on IFRS.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The semaglutide validation fails again or Canada prices collapse as generics multiply; abatacept gets FDA queries or a re-inspection and slips a year; US base erosion continues (~US$900 mn); Russia slows; margins stay near Q1FY27's level.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Dr. Reddy's: P/E on one-year-forward EPS (MOSL 20x 12m fwd, PL 23x FY28E, ICICI Direct 22x FY28E, BOB 21x Jun-28E, Elara 28x FY28E core EPS plus cash, ICICI Securities 20x FY28E). Our multiple: Dr. Reddy's own one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 on EPS before one-off items (trough years excluded) x the pharma sector factor (+8.2%, the median of the nine-peer set, PLAYBOOK §7c), nearest half-turn; bull = 75th percentile x factor, bear = 25th percentile x factor. Written by tools/authoring/DRREDDY.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021 (EV from Screener's EV multiple x trailing EBITDA; forward EBITDA on Screener's basis before impairments and the FY26 specific items) x the nine peers' EV/EBITDA factor, nearest half-turn; plus the engine's net cash at Sep-28E (DRREDDY.ctx.js).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether Dr. Reddy's cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, cost of equity 11.6%, terminal growth 5.5%, plus the engine's net cash at Mar-27.
